problem: Suppose we are applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{1}:=18{R}_{1}$ to a $2\times 2$ matrix $A.$ Find the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication.

activity_context.topic_title: Row Operations on 2x2 Matrices as Products of Elementary Matrices

examples.knowledge_point: Finding a Matrix Product That's Equivalent To a Given Row Operation
examples.problem: Suppose we are applying the elementary row operation $R_1:=R_1 - R_2$ to a $2\times 2$ matrix $A.$ Find the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication.
examples.worked_solution:
We need to find an elementary matrix $E$ such that $EA$ is equivalent to applying the elementary row operation $R_1:=R_1 - R_2$ to $A.$

To find $E,$ we apply the given row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}-{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =E\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication is $EA\mathbin{:}$

feedback.problem: Let $E=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -10\end{aligned}].$ Find the row operation that, when applied to a $2\times 2$ matrix $A,$ gives the result of the product $EA.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The given matrix $E$ is obtained by multiplying the second row of the identity matrix by $-10$: 

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-10{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -10\end{aligned}] \\  & =E\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $EA$ is equivalent to applying the row operation  ${R}_{2}:=-10{R}_{2}$ to $A.$
